handback.t:
R4-A1 (prefix h1) is finished. All numbers are synthetic until validated on real traffic. Full detail with VERIFY REQUEST blocks and rerun commands is in `C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\h1_board_entry.md`. The full lib test passes (286/286, `--test-threads 2`). I edited only `src/embedding.rs`, `src/memory.rs` and my own bins/results. I did not touch the director's Cargo.toml. No commits.

**1. HNSW fix re-bench (before = unpatched copy under `C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r1/copy`, after = repo build)**
- **Systematic loss:** items that are not their own top-1 drop from 0.68-1.08 % to 0 in every wrapper path and cell, and recall@10 improves.

  | cell | recall@10 before -> after |
  |---|---|
  | N2000 d32 iid | .983 -> .999 |
  | N2000 d32 clustered | .989 -> 1.000 |
  | N5000 d128 clustered | .988 -> 1.000 |
  | N5000 d384 iid (ef64, hard regime) | .659 -> .671 |

  - The paths covered are `HnswIndex.add`, `add_batch`, `HnswRm` (including remove-10 % + compact), `workmem::Store(Hnsw)`, `TieredMemory`, `LessonStore` and `CaseRouter::with_index`.
  - Unretrievable cases/lessons (~0.6-1.1 % before) go to 0.
  - In my easy downstream worlds the posterior error drops 100x, but decisions are visibly unchanged.
- **Existing bins:** `memory_bench` and `r3_store` at 10k vectors show recall at ef64 going from .987 to 1.000, and the old .992 ceiling at ef256 is gone.
- **Cost:** HNSW build time is +22-29 % at 5k-10k vectors and unchanged at 2k. Query latency is unchanged and heap is the same.
- **Unit test:** `memory::tests::hnsw_loses_no_items_n2000_d32_several_seeds` passes with the fix and fails on the unpatched copy (14 lost in the first build). I could not make it an exact 0 on every build because of the new finding below. It allows at most 2 lossy builds out of 17, which flakes about 1e-4 per run.
- **New finding, not fixed:** the fixed crate still has a rare second failure mode. About 0.5 % of builds (14 of 2548, 95 % CI .3-.9 %) lose 8-37 % of the items; recall@10 is about .67 in those builds.
  - The unpatched crate showed 4 of 2548 (0.16 %); the difference is p = .03, post-hoc, so not established as caused by the fix.
  - `keep_pruned`, `extend_candidates` and larger efc did not remove it; M32 showed 0 of 500, which is too few to claim anything.
  - I did not root-cause it.
  - It also showed up once in 8 builds in `memory_lab --quick`.
- **Mitigation I added (opt-in):** `HnswIndex::audit`, `rebuild` and `audit_and_repair`. Over 2000 builds it detected 8 of 8 bad builds with 0 false alarms, and one rebuild repaired all 8. An audit of 200 samples costs about 5 % of the build time.
- **For dependents:** `[patch.crates-io]` only applies in the workspace root. A new `hnsw_integrity_probe` lets a dependent crate detect the unpatched crate.

**2. Compute-once embedding (`MemoEmbedding` and `Embedded` in `src/embedding.rs`)**
- **Where duplicates are:** `ResearchSession`, `KnowledgeRouter`, serve, tiered and lessons encode a task once or take ready vectors. The duplicates are in compositions. A `Warm<CaseRouter>` + `Knowledge` stack calls the encoder 3.64 times per decision. `coupling.rs` also hash-embeds twice, but in a different space, so it is not shareable.
- **Wiring:** `task_embedder()` returns exactly the `casebased::Embedder` closure type, so no changes are needed in other files.
- **Encoder calls per decision:** 3.64 (baseline) -> 0.98 (per-decision memo, cap 4) -> 0.39 (cap 4096, over repeat-heavy streams). A world with no repeats gets 1.00 with either memo.
- **Bit-identity:** decisions are identical across all arms on 30 seeds x 10 worlds x 2 encoders (MiniLM table and hash). The comparison covers anchor, agent, reward, retrieval hits with similarity bits, a stream digest and final posteriors. The reward model is my own, not f6's.
- **Latency:** with a cheap encoder the memo is neutral to +14 % per decision, and the existing `CachedEmbedding` is +19 %. At the modelled 2.4 ms/text the cost per decision is 8.7 -> 2.4 -> 0.95 ms. The 8.7 ms is a model; only the simulated 2.4 ms busy-wait row is wall-clock (7.9 -> 2.4 ms).
- **Bytes:** about 1.7 KB per entry at d384.

**3. Query-embedding and result cache (`CachedIndex` in `src/memory.rs`, plus `impl MemoryIndex for Box<T>`)**
- **Invalidation:** the default clears the cache on any write. `.selective(true)` is for exact-score backends only.
- **Correctness:** 0 stale results across every query of every stream (Flat and HNSW, with and without writes). Two unit tests also cover it. On Flat, all cache arms return identical (id, score-bits) lists. For HNSW, cached-answer recall@5 minus inner-answer recall@5 is at worst +0.0000 (vs exact Flat truth at the same write state).
- **Saving:** on a 93 %-repeat stream, modelled cost per query goes 2.48 -> 0.25 ms with the embedding memo alone (-90 %) and -> 0.18 ms with the result cache too (-93 %). Zipf gives -79 % and mixed50 -45 %. A stream with no repeats shows 0.0 % change on Flat; on HNSW it is within noise (-0.6 to +1.6 %, +0.8 on the selective arm).
- **Writes:** clear-all collapses the result-cache hit rate from .928 to .083 when there is one write per 50 queries; selective mode keeps it at .928.
- **Caveats:**
  - The saving is almost all the embedding memo.
  - The result cache only saves a search of about 100 µs here.
  - Hit rates depend on exact-vector repeats, and the templated synthetic corpus repeats more than real traffic probably does.

- `results/h1_proposed_patch.md`: optional wiring in `research.rs`, `serve.rs` and `tiered.rs`, and the audit call sites for `HnswRm::compact` and workmem `Store`.
- Raw logs, CSVs and JSONs are in `results/h1_*`. The bins are `src/bin/h1_hnsw.rs`, `h1_hnsw_probe.rs`, `h1_embed.rs` and `h1_cache.rs`.
